report.tagline: OpenAI's AI video app, a TikTok-style feed of generated clips, which launched in September 2025 and was shut down in March 2026.
report.simpleSummary: Sora was an app from OpenAI where you typed a short idea and AI made a 10-second video with sound. You could put yourself or friends into videos using a feature called cameos, and scroll a feed of everyone's AI videos, like TikTok. It went viral and hit number one on the App Store in its first week. But downloads fell fast, each video was very costly to make, deepfake worries grew, and OpenAI shut the app down in March 2026.

overview.whatItDoes: Sora let users make short AI videos with sound from a text prompt, remix other people's videos and add real people through verified cameos. Videos appeared in a scrollable feed with likes, comments and follows. OpenAI hoped it would win attention, and later ad money, from TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. The app is now closed.
howItWorks: Sign up with an OpenAI account, at first by invite code.
Type a prompt such as 'a cat doing a cricket commentary' and Sora 2 makes a 10-second clip with audio.
Record a short verification video to create a cameo, so you and friends you allow can appear in videos.
Scroll the feed, like, comment, and remix any video.
Free users got a daily number of generations; extra ones could be bought.
All videos carried a visible watermark and hidden labels saying they were AI-made.
overview.valueProposition: Make funny, shareable videos starring you and your friends in seconds, with no camera or editing skill.

painPoints.pain: Making a funny or creative video needs filming and editing skills.
painPoints.howSolved: Sora made a full clip with sound from one sentence.

painPoints.pain: Putting yourself in a fantasy scene was impossible without effects skills.
painPoints.howSolved: Cameos placed your face and voice into any video.
A feed of AI videos offered new, strange content, at least at first.

painPoints.pain: People fear their likeness being used without permission.
painPoints.howSolved: Cameo controls let users choose who could use their likeness, but critics said protections were not enough.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Sora 2 made short, realistic or cartoon videos with speech and sound effects.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The wow moment that drove early downloads.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Verified users could add themselves and friends into videos.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Made videos personal and social, the main reason people shared them.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Change any video in the feed with a new prompt.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Created chains of trends, like a social network.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A TikTok-style feed with likes, comments and follows.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: OpenAI's attempt to build a social product and future ad business.
Needed for safety, but easy to crop, which fed deepfake worries.

steps.detail: A wild Sora video shows up on Instagram.
Finds an invite code from a friend.
Records a short face and voice check.
Makes clips of friends as cricket stars and movie heroes.
Downloads and posts them on Reels and WhatsApp.
After two or three weeks, stops opening the app.
Tries effects for a video intro.
Character prompts get blocked after rights holder complaints.
Switches to Veo, Kling or Runway for longer clips.
OpenAI posts 'saying goodbye to the Sora app' on 24 March 2026.
Waits for OpenAI's instructions to save creations.
Uses AI video tools inside other apps, like Meta AI or Gemini.

businessModel.summary: Sora barely made money. The app was free, with limited sales of extra generations and Sora access through ChatGPT paid plans. The plan was to grow a huge feed and later sell ads, but each video cost a lot to make and users did not stay long enough to build an ad business.

revenueStreams.detail: Users could buy more videos after hitting the free daily limit.
Plus and Pro subscribers got more and higher-quality Sora use.
A Disney deal brought its characters to Sora; Disney also invested in OpenAI.
Ads in the feed were the long-term goal but never became a real business.

businessModel.pricing: Free with daily limits; extra generations sold in small packs; more use with ChatGPT Plus ($20 a month) and Pro ($200 a month). App closed in 2026.
costDrivers: GPU computing for each video, far more than for a text answer
Content moderation and safety teams to stop deepfakes and abuse
Legal risk from copyright holders and estates
Storage and streaming of millions of videos
businessModel.unitEconomics: A 10-second AI video might cost OpenAI somewhere around $0.50 to $2 in computing, many times a text answer. A free user making 20 videos a day could cost $10 to $40 a day while paying nothing. To cover that with ads, a user would need to watch a lot, but most users stopped after a few weeks. So each active user likely lost money. These are rough outside estimates, not OpenAI figures.

howTheyGetUsers: Viral clips shared on TikTok, Instagram and X
Invite codes that created scarcity and buzz
OpenAI's brand and ChatGPT's huge user base
Cameos: users invited friends so they could appear together
whatBringsUsersBack: Friends tagging you in new cameo videos
Trends and remix chains in the feed
growth.moat: Sora had little moat. Rival models like Google's Veo, Kling and Runway soon matched quality, and AI video features appeared inside apps people already used, like Instagram and YouTube. A feed needs a lasting habit, which Sora never built.

competitors.name: TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts
competitors.positioning: Huge short video platforms with real creators.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Sora had only AI videos, which felt fun at first but less meaningful than real people.

competitors.name: Google Veo (in Gemini and YouTube)
competitors.positioning: AI video built into Google's apps.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Google offered similar quality where users already were.

competitors.name: Meta AI and Vibes
competitors.positioning: AI video feed and tools inside Meta's apps.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Meta had billions of users and an ad business ready to pay for it.

competitors.name: Kling, Runway and Pika
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: They focus on creative tools, not a social feed.

northStar.why: A good north star for a social app shows both sides: people keep creating and others keep watching. This captures both sides of the network.

guardrailMetrics: Share of feed that users rate as low quality ('AI slop')
strengths: Strong AI video model with sound (Sora 2)
Clever cameo feature that made videos social
Visible watermarks and provenance labels from day one
weaknesses: Very high cost per video with little revenue
Novelty faded quickly; downloads fell about 45 percent within months
A feed of only AI videos lacked the human connection of TikTok
Safety and copyright rules changed reactively after complaints
risks: Deepfake harm and regulation on synthetic media
Copyright claims from studios, estates and actors' unions
Big platforms adding AI video for free
Distraction from OpenAI's core business when computing is scarce
userComplaints: Deepfakes of real people, including dead celebrities like Martin Luther King Jr. and Michael Jackson, before OpenAI restricted them
Daily limits and short clip length
Rules on characters and likeness kept changing
Disappointment and worry about losing creations when the app shut down

improvementIdeas.idea: Opt-in likeness controls by default, so no real person can appear unless they have verified and approved
improvementIdeas.problem: Deepfakes of public figures and others harmed trust.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer harmful videos and less legal risk.

improvementIdeas.idea: Build Sora as a creation tool inside ChatGPT and other apps instead of a separate social feed
improvementIdeas.problem: Users did not form a habit of opening a standalone AI video feed.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher use with less cost of building a network from scratch.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Videos created per weekly ChatGPT user

improvementIdeas.idea: Charge per video from the start, with a small free allowance
improvementIdeas.problem: Free videos cost too much to serve.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Revenue minus computing cost per active user

improvementIdeas.idea: Group challenges and private friend feeds instead of a public feed
improvementIdeas.problem: Public AI content felt like slop; the fun was with friends.

pmLessons: A viral launch is not product-market fit. Watch retention after week one, not downloads.
Check unit economics early. If each use costs a lot and users pay nothing, growth makes losses bigger.
Safety must be designed in from day one, not added after public outcry.
Social apps need a reason to return. Novelty fades; friends and meaning keep people coming back.

interviewQuestions.question: Sora hit number one on the App Store and shut down six months later. Why?
interviewQuestions.hint: Cover retention (novelty faded), unit economics (costly videos, little revenue), safety (deepfakes) and competition (AI video in existing apps).

interviewQuestions.question: If you were the PM in October 2025, what metrics would have warned you?
interviewQuestions.hint: Week-4 retention, videos per user versus cost, share of feed views from friends, deepfake reports. Explain what each signals.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you design consent for putting real people in AI videos?
interviewQuestions.hint: Verification, opt-in permission per person, revoke anytime, notifications when used, quick takedown. Balance fun and safety.

interviewQuestions.question: Should OpenAI have built Sora as a standalone app or inside ChatGPT?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare reach, habit and cost. Standalone gives a social network chance; inside ChatGPT uses existing users. Recommend one with reasons.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you make an AI video product profitable?
interviewQuestions.hint: Target users who pay (creators, marketers), charge per video, cut cost per video, and sell to businesses. Track margin per user.
